title: Vitruvian tool manifest
description: The file vitruvian-tool.json at the top of a tool's folder. It says what the tool is, which of the app's services it calls, what it adds, and which program to start. A field this schema does not name is ignored, which is how a later version adds one. Four rules are not written here because JSON Schema cannot say them: no two commands, no two panels and no two preferences share an id; the whole file is at most 65,536 bytes; no two options of one preference share a value; and a preference with options has a default that is one of them.

id.description: The tool's identity, in reverse-DNS form, for example com.acme.deploys. Letters, digits, hyphens and underscores in parts joined by single dots. It must have a dot: an id with none belongs to a feature built into the app. At most 128 characters. It never changes between versions of a tool.

name.description: What the tool is called, shown as written.

description.description: One sentence on what the tool does, shown as written.

version.description: The tool's own version, as its author writes it.

protocol.description: The protocol version the tool speaks. Version 2 adds panels, what a tool draws, and changes nothing of version 1. An app that speaks only version 1 refuses a manifest that says 2.

publisher.description: Who made the tool. Shown beside its name. The app does not check it.

license.description: The licence the tool is offered under, for example an SPDX identifier.

icon.description: An SF Symbol name. A name this Mac does not have draws as a plain puzzle piece.

uses.description: The app services the tool calls. The app refuses a call to a service that is not listed. This is not a list of what the tool is allowed to do: a tool is a separate program and can do anything the app can.

contributes.description: What the tool adds to the app.

preferences.description: The settings the tool keeps through the app. At most 16.

activation.description: When the app starts the tool. onCommand: the first time one of its commands runs. onLaunch: with the app. Left out, it is onCommand.

allOf.description: Panels are protocol 2's: a manifest that says 1 contributes none, not even an empty list.
A status is protocol 2's too: a manifest that says 1 declares none.

localizedText.description: A piece of text in one or more languages, keyed by language tag (en, fr, pt-BR). English, under en, is required. The app shows the entry for the language in use, then the entry for that language without its region, then English.

contributes.description: What the tool adds to the app: commands, and in protocol 2 panels and a status.

panels.description: What the tool draws, and where. At most 8; at most one in the island and one in Settings. Protocol 2 only.

status.description: The tool shows a status: a small mark the app draws, which the tool sets with ui/status. Without this, the app refuses ui/status. Protocol 2 only. An app before 3.48 ignores it, and shows no status.

statusContribution.description: That the tool shows a status, and where.

placement.description: Where it is shown. island: on the closed island, beside the agent mark.

activity.description: true: the tool's status may carry words for the closed island, and the agreement sheet says so. An app before 3.50 ignores it.

command.description: One thing the tool can be asked to do.

id.description: The command's name within the tool. The same characters as a tool id; a dot is not needed. The app knows the command as <tool id>/<this id>.

title.description: What the command is called in a list.

icon.description: An SF Symbol name. Left out, the tool's icon is used.

surfaces.description: Where the command is offered: the command bar, the radial menu, the Quick panel, and as a shortcut the person records.

panel.description: One place the tool draws in. The app opens it with ui/open and the tool answers with blocks to draw; or, for a web panel, the app shows the page at entry.

id.description: The panel's name within the tool. The same characters as a command id.

title.description: What the panel is called: the island page's title, the window's title.

placement.description: Where it is shown. island: a page in the island's Tools area. settings: a part of the tool's detail in Settings. window: a window the app owns, opened when the person asks.

icon.description: An SF Symbol name. Left out, the tool's icon is used.

kind.description: What draws it. blocks: the app, from blocks the tool sends. web: a web page from the tool's folder. Left out, it is blocks.

entry.description: A web panel's page, as a path inside the tool's folder, with / between its parts. No part is empty, . or .., so the path cannot leave the folder. A blocks panel ignores it.

preference.description: One setting. The tool reads and writes it with storage/get and storage/set. The person sees and changes it in the tool's detail in Settings when it has a title, and the tool is then sent preferences/changed.

id.description: The setting's name within the tool. The same characters as a command id.

title.description: What the setting is called where the person changes it, shown as written. At most 60 characters in each language, with no line break and no other control character. Left out, the app does not show the setting: the tool alone reads and writes it. An app older than this field ignores it, and shows no setting.

type.description: What kind of value it holds.

default.description: The value before anything is saved. It is of the type named.

options.description: The values the person chooses among: the app draws the setting as a pop-up menu, not a field. From 1 to 64, no two with one value, and the default is one of them. Only a string preference may have them. They are how the app draws, not a rule on the value: a saved value that is no option's is kept and shown as written. An app before 3.48 ignores them, and draws a text field.

allOf.description: Options are a text setting's: a preference of another type has none.

preferenceOption.description: One value a preference with options may be set to, and what the person reads for it.

value.description: What is saved when the person picks it. At most 128 characters, with no line break and no other control character. It may be empty.

title.description: What the menu shows for it, as written. Held to what a preference's title is: at most 60 characters in each language, with no line break and no other control character.

kind.description: external: a separate program. The only kind a manifest file may name.

exec.description: The program, as a path inside the tool's folder, with / between its parts. No part is empty, . or .., so the path cannot leave the folder.
